speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, the IDA empowers MOH to conduct surveillance for infectious diseases, isolate and treat the infected persons and quarantine close contacts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The IDA also allows us to investigate and manage outbreaks with measures, such as contact tracing and disinfection of premises.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: IDA has been an effective piece of legislation and saw Singapore through health crises, such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) in 2003 and H1N1 in 2009.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Between influenza and SARS, COVID-19 is somewhere in-between.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It had a case fatality rate of about 2% to 5% when it first emerged, far higher than influenza, but lower than SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, COVID-19 was far more infectious than SARS, spreading via airborne droplets and by infected persons yet to display symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It became clear that we were facing a new enemy and it was no longer sufficient to solely rely on the approach of "test, trace, isolate", our main takeaway during SARS, to fight this new virus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Nationwide restrictions and community-based measures became necessary to curtail disease spread, reduce deaths and safeguard our healthcare system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As different variants emerged and various infection waves hit us, Part 7 enabled the implementation of many measures, including the circuit breaker, various gradations of safe management measures (SMMs), vaccination-differentiated SMMs and it also facilitated the implementation of TraceTogether and SafeEntry systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As our population was increasingly protected by vaccinations and safe recovery from infections, we cautiously reopened our society and economy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Part 7 continued to provide the agility and allow us to calibrate our SMMs and to ease restrictions according to risk assessments.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Government conducted a comprehensive review of our responses during the COVID-19 pandemic crisis and its findings were released as a White Paper and debated in this House in March 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: One of the key recommendations of the White Paper was the need to review and amend the IDA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: COVID-19 is not going to be the last pandemic and we need better and permanent tools for the next threat.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The pandemic has given us fresh perspectives on the management of infectious disease threats, and our laws, namely the IDA, needs to be reviewed and be ready for the next pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In this comprehensive review of the IDA, various Part 7 powers that continue to be relevant to future pandemic responses will be ported over to the IDA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have also taken this opportunity to streamline the legislation, iron out kinks and make provisions for operational effectiveness by drawing lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I will introduce the key substantive amendments in the Bill in my speech.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Thereafter, I will pass the time to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam to elaborate on the other amendments to the IDA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The main change to the IDA is to provide for a hierarchy of responses to address outbreaks of differing severity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This was a key takeaway from COVID-19, when we had to step-up responses as the situation escalated and taper down measures when the threat subsided.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We need the IDA to provide the Minister for Health the powers to effect relevant measures at different phases of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It only provides for the declaration of a Public Health Emergency (PHE) by the Minister for Health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This was not declared during COVID-19 because while the pandemic situation was dire, we felt it fell short of an emergency – partly also due to the way we had managed the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We would associate an emergency with more extreme situations, like widespread riots, or war; or in the context of a pandemic, a healthcare system that is totally overwhelmed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will also provide the powers for the Minister to respond appropriately, based on each situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Minister may declare a PHT if he or she is satisfied that the actual or likely incidence and transmission of an infectious disease in Singapore constitutes a serious threat to public health and it is necessary to take measures to prevent, protect against, delay or control such incidence or transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The outbreak of COVID-19 in Singapore in 2020 would have been considered a PHT under the new provisions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Minister will also have the powers to make regulations to implement measures to respond to the PHT as we had.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These include movement restrictions; prohibitions of gatherings or events beyond a specified group size; or the suspension of non-essential businesses; up to and including a circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All these powers are currently found in Part 7 and will be ported over to the IDA, as powers under a PHT – a threat.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A PHE will trigger powers in the most dire of situations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Declaration of a PHE is already an existing provision in the IDA, but we are finetuning the criteria of a PHE and proposing to make adjustments to the powers of the Minister under this situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have enhanced the existing criteria for the declaration of a PHE, by factoring in the state of our healthcare systems and resources, in addition to the epidemiology of the disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A PHE declaration, if done, will unlock two additional powers for the Minister for Health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These are envisioned to be much more stringent than the measures, including a circuit breaker, provided under a PHT.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, the Minister may impose an island-wide curfew during specific time periods of the day or limit the number of persons that may leave a home every day.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: During COVID-19, some countries had imposed such curfew-like measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, in parts of India, persons were restricted from leaving the home overnight; and some China provinces restricted the number of persons per household who could leave the home and then only to obtain necessities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fortunately, we did not need to impose any of these highly-restrictive measures during COVID-19, partly because our hospitals, while strained and stressed, were never overwhelmed like in many other countries where a big number of patients had to be left unattended.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we cannot be complacent and assume that we will be as fortunate in the next pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is a need to be ready for a situation where more stringent measures are needed to avoid a public health catastrophe.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The RORA can already be exercised by the Minister for Defence during a PHE.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: What we will be doing with the amendments to the IDA is to also allow the Minister for Health to exercise requisition powers in a PHE.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is consistent with the overall objective of RORA, one of which is to provide for requisition of resources as necessary for the securing of the safety of human life and health in the event of a PHE.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We can envision that in a situation when Disease X strikes, the Minister may need to acquire private hospital beds, medical equipment, ambulances and manpower to shore up resources to tend to our population who may otherwise not be able to receive care expediently.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Parties affected by such requisitions will be appropriately compensated under the RORA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Drawing from our experience with epidemic waves – including that of COVID-19 – 90 days will provide sufficient time for the effect of measures to kick in and for MOH to review and assess the impact on the public health situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the situation subsides early, the declaration may be revoked early.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The measures under a PHT and PHE can be intrusive and disruptive, so they need to be triggered only when necessary to protect lives.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These decisions will only be taken, following careful consideration based on prevailing scientific evidence and risk assessments and at the highest level of Government.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Minister must first, by order, declare a PHT or PHE and publish a notice to bring the order to the public's attention.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All orders to declare or extend a PHT or PHE and any regulations made during a PHT or PHE, must be published in the Gazette and presented to Parliament as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Parliament has the authority to scrutinise the order or regulations and if unsatisfied with the decisions, vote to annul them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To sum up, what I have just described can be found under clause 22 of the Bill, which inserts into the IDA a new Part 3A on the control of infectious disease during a PHT and PHE.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Further details on amendments to enhance operational efficiency during a PHT and PHE will be elaborated on by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In effect, with these amendments, our public health response will comprise four postures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a peacetime state where routine disease prevention and control measures, along with public health surveillance programmes, are in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: During peacetime, the primary objective is to detect outbreaks early to prevent and mitigate disease spread.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, "Outbreak Management", where there are signs of an emerging infectious disease overseas, upstream measures, such as pre-departure health requirements, temperature screening or stay orders on persons entering Singapore, may be implemented to prevent the disease from being introduced into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will help prevent disease importation and transmission and buy us time to understand the new disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the event of a local outbreak, measures such as testing, treatment and contact tracing, may be implemented.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is what we did recently at Bukit Merah due to a local tuberculosis outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The IDA does not explicitly mention "Baseline" and "Outbreak Management" situation tiers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These measures are already well-established and routinely carried out and for these two tiers, they are already legally backed by various sections in the IDA; but these two are useful lexicons for us to remember.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These four public health postures will inform the application of the IDA henceforth and will greatly facilitate nimbler management of different stages of an outbreak or pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As part of this Bill, the Government will be proposing the repeal of Part 11 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, in short, I will refer to it as Part 11.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Part 11 was introduced in 2021 to provide assurance to the public that personal contact tracing data collected during digital contact tracing systems, including TraceTogether and SafeEntry were limited for the purposes of contact tracing for COVID-19 and for criminal investigations and proceedings in respect of serious offences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: TraceTogether and SafeEntry have not been active for about a year as we transitioned to treating COVID-19 as an endemic disease and SMMs were stepped down.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, as the Minister charged with the responsibility for digital Government and public sector data governance, in consultation with MOH, determined that these digital contact tracing systems would no longer be required after 5 January 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: TraceTogether and SafeEntry have since been removed from the app stores and the backend digital infrastructure supporting the TraceTogether and SafeEntry systems have been dismantled.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The TraceTogether and SafeEntry websites have also been shut down.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for the future, with the rapid advancement of digital technology, precision medicine and artificial intelligence, it may not be wise to pre-judge what we may or can do in future pandemics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We may collect different kinds of data digitally.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We may use them differently to fight the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The public may need new forms of assurances.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Part 11 is bound to be obsolete when the next pandemic hits us.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the event of a future pandemic crisis and should we implement a digital personal data collection tool to be part of our arsenal to fight the pandemic, we will need to address data protection concerns and provide assurance to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To do so, the Government will come back to Parliament to pass legislation, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the meantime, we will closely monitor the technologies available, their possible use cases and relevance for future pandemics.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will allow us to quickly determine, at the onset of the next outbreak, whether and what tools should be deployed as well as the relevant safeguards to be implemented to ensure that an individual's personal data are used with discernment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I will now pass the time to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Ms Rahayu Mahzam to elaborate on these amendments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides the Minister's powers to make regulations during a PHT or PHE, the following amendments are also being introduced to enhance operational and enforcement efficiency during a PHT or PHE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Two, oral directions may be given by authorised Health Officers to require persons to comply with the relevant PHT or PHE regulations in force.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, if there is a regulation that imposes limits on the size of gatherings and a Health Officer comes across a gathering that exceeds this limit, the Health Officer may give an oral direction to the group requiring them to disperse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The effectiveness of disease containment efforts is contingent on the public's cooperation in taking public health measures seriously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Non-compliance does not only put oneself at risk of disease, but also others in the community and can set our national efforts back significantly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members of the public will still be able to reach out to MOH to seek exceptional handling on a case-by-case basis, and MOH will attend to these quickly and administratively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These amendments will allow the expeditious implementation of public health measures during a PHT or PHE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides incorporating the relevant powers under Part 7 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act and providing a gradation of responses under the IDA, MOH has also taken this opportunity to review and update the IDA in its entirety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has required us to adopt new ways to prevent, mitigate and manage infectious disease outbreaks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Advancements in scientific technology and ever-growing international connectivity have demonstrated the need for a new paradigm of infectious disease management measures to fit the modern times.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Public health actions under the IDA are mainly carried out by the Health Officers appointed by the Director-General of Health, the Director-General of Public Health, or the Director-General, Food Administration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the powers exercisable under the IDA may potentially be intrusive, only public officers, officers of statutory bodies and employees of prescribed institutions, may currently be appointed as Health Officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, manpower from the public service forms a relatively smaller portion of the local workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: When faced with a pandemic, there is often the need to tap on the rest of the workforce to supplement the national response.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With diverse partnerships or working arrangements, less intrusive functions can be performed by other parties in partnership with the public service.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The first new group of persons are employees of prescribed entities and institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These will include employees of private healthcare providers and MOH-linked entities such as MOH Holdings and the Agency for Integrated Care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The second new group are employees of prescribed service providers that the Government or statutory bodies have engaged.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These could include call centres engaged to do contact tracing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These three groups were in fact closest to the action during the COVID-19 pandemic, and will be the first sources of manpower MOH will tap on, especially during an escalating outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As public sector resources will be stretched further during a PHT or PHE, there may be a need to bring together additional manpower to supplement and support these Health Officers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clause 22 introduces a new section 21I of the Bill, which will allow persons who are deemed suitable to be appointed as adjunct Health Officers during a PHT or PHE, to perform the functions of a Health Officer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These persons could include volunteers, such as former nurses, who have stepped forward to help with contact tracing and surveillance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To ensure proper oversight over these Health Officers and adjunct Health Officers, they will need to be appointed and authorised with powers on an as-needed basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They will also be informed of the scope of their powers and the validity period of their appointments and receive appropriate training before being tasked to carry out their functions under the IDA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The IDA also provides for specific situations where the arrest of offenders may be carried out by authorised Health Officers without a warrant, such as the arrest of persons who breach isolation orders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH recognises that the power of arrest is a serious one which should only be exercised by persons who are trained to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Accordingly, clauses 14 and 36, and the new section 21H of the Bill, insert an additional safeguard where only Health Officers who are public officers, officers of statutory bodies and auxiliary police officers can be authorised to arrest persons without a warrant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, these officers must also be separately authorised by the Minister to exercise such powers of arrest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also will be strengthening our levers to safeguard our population against the importation of disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Global connectivity in modern times can facilitate the spread and migration of diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Outbreaks in one country can spread rapidly to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Given that Singapore is an international trade and travel hub, we remain vulnerable to the importation of emerging infectious diseases and must take the necessary precautions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Many would be familiar with the concept of pre-departure testing and mask-wearing on international flights implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Upon arrival, travellers may also be required to produce proof of their compliance with any pre-departure health requirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Non-compliance with any of these requirements can give rise to an offence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clause 27 of the Bill will provide us with the ability to impose such requirements uniformly and to take firm action against incoming travellers who do not comply with them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, section 31 of the IDA requires persons arriving in Singapore by air or sea to fulfil specified vaccination requirements and show proof of such vaccination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In line with the World Health Organization’s (WHO's) recommendations, this provision is currently applied in respect of yellow fever vaccinations for travellers from certain African and South American countries that are endemic for yellow fever.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is intended to protect Singapore against the risk of importation of the disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such medical examinations, also known as "exit-screening", are implemented in advance of a PHT or PHE as a key measure to prevent the cross-border spread of an infectious disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such measures are also in line with the WHO’s recommendations under the International Health Regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore is a densely populated country, and this can accelerate the spread of an infectious disease within the population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, additionally, we will be strengthening our levers to prevent disease transmission within our communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, the IDA recognises three categories of persons in relation to an infectious disease: one, actual infected "cases" who have the disease; two, "carriers" who are harbouring, likely to or suspected of harbouring the disease; and three, "contacts" who have been exposed to the risk of infection from the disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An "at-risk individual" includes an individual who is or appears to the Director-General of Health or a Health Officer to be a contact or carrier of an infectious disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Examples of such individuals include those who live in high-risk living arrangements or work in high-risk occupations where prolonged close contact with others may be unavoidable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An "at-risk individual" would also include individuals entering Singapore from a country during a period when there is an outbreak or suspected outbreak in that country.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Individuals who have undergone a medical examination in connection with an infectious disease but have not received a conclusive test result are also "at-risk individuals".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The recognition of "at-risk individuals" and the application of the powers under the IDA to such individuals allow public health measures, such as testing or isolation, to be carried out at an early stage to stem the spread of an infectious disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, there were instances where persons who were served with isolation orders went about running errands or having meals, before heading home to be isolated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such actions have heightened the risk of disease transmission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clause 12 of the Bill introduces a new provision that makes it an offence if such persons, without reasonable cause, fail to proceed to the place of isolation as soon as possible, if the isolation order does not specify a time to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, section 21A of the IDA requires persons who know or have reason to suspect that they are a case, carrier or contact of a dangerous infectious disease to not expose others to the risk of infection in places outside of their homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Household members inherently face higher transmission risk, and the current provision assumes that they are willing to accept such risks due to their close relationship or living arrangements with one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, the COVID-19 pandemic showed us that there can be varied living arrangements in Singapore where the assumption may not apply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This would allow us to act against infected persons who refuse to isolate in their rooms or continue to use communal areas without taking reasonable precautions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Various provisions in the IDA will also be refined to meet our operational needs in managing the outbreak of infectious diseases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clause 3 of the Bill introduces a new section 2A, which provides that, one, parents or guardians of minors and, two, guardians of persons with any intellectual disability or lacking in mental capacity, may be notified of any requirement, direction, notice or order that has been issued to the person under their care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Upon receipt of such notice, the parent or guardian will be personally required to ensure that the person under their care complies with the requirement, direction, notice or order, as the case may be.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, section 17 of the IDA requires the declaration of an isolation area to be published in the Gazette before it can take effect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Clause 14 of the Bill amends section 17 to provide that the declaration of an isolation area takes effect once it is brought to the notice of all persons who need to be aware of the declaration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This amendment will allow for the effective and timely isolation of persons within a particular area to prevent the spread of disease.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For public awareness, MOH will continue to publish the declaration of an isolation area in the Gazette.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The IDA will also be updated to account for the latest modalities and approaches to disease management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, the definition of "medical examination" in section 2 of the IDA will be expanded to include self-administered examinations such as antigen-rapid tests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Separately, for clarity, the service of orders and notices under the IDA using electronic means such as email and SMS will also be explicitly recognised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These amendments are in recognition that such decisions would be better suited to the professional expertise of the Director-General.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These powers include imposing requirements on healthcare professionals or institutions for the purposes of investigating or preventing the spread of an infectious disease; the declaration of isolation areas; and orders to disseminate health advisories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH will be removing the requirement which circumscribes the group of persons who can perform vaccinations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The provision of vaccination, including the persons who may perform vaccinations, will be regulated under relevant levers that govern healthcare service delivery and the conduct of practitioners, such as the Healthcare Services Act 2020 and the Medical Registration Act 1997.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Section 23(1) of the IDA was introduced in 1992 as one of the public health measures to control and curb HIV transmission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It requires persons living with HIV to inform their sexual partners, prior to sexual activity, of the risk of contracting HIV from them and to obtain the partner’s consent to accept the risk of transmission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This allows the sexual partner to make an informed decision on whether to proceed with the sexual activity and take necessary precautions to minimise the risk of contracting HIV.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In practice, doctors regularly inform patients about this legal obligation at the point of HIV diagnosis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The intention of this disclosure requirement was to control the spread of HIV and deter the irresponsible behaviour of those that put others at risk of contracting HIV.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The disclosure requirement remains relevant as a public health safeguard to protect the sexual partners of persons living with HIV.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Section 23(2) of the IDA similarly requires persons who do not know that they have HIV but have reason to believe that they may have HIV, to inform their sexual partners of the risk of infection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These safeguards remain and will continue to deter irresponsible behaviour, including from those who attempt to hide behind the ignorance of their HIV status.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While the safeguards are in place to deter irresponsible behaviour, it is important also for our HIV legislation to be aligned with medical advancements in HIV treatment, in order to encourage early detection and treatment of HIV.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, with medical advancements in HIV treatment, persons living with HIV who adhere to their HIV treatment as prescribed by their doctors are now able to reduce the amount of HIV in their bodies to an undetectable level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is referred to as having an undetectable viral load.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A person who maintains a stable undetectable viral load over time, as a result of a consistent adherence to their treatment, cannot transmit HIV to their sexual partner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The sexual partner therefore is not at risk of contracting HIV from these individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The objectives of the amendments are to encourage individuals who are at high risk of getting HIV to be tested regularly for HIV, and if possible, to get treated early, so that they can achieve undetectable viral load as early as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We urge persons living with HIV to adhere to HIV treatment and monitor their viral load closely with their doctors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In doing so, we aim to reduce the risk of HIV transmission.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore is not the first or only country to amend the law on this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Irresponsible behaviour that can lead to the transmission of HIV remains an offence in Singapore and appropriate enforcement action will be taken as required.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To conclude, I return to the primary aim behind the amendment Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As experts have cautioned, the likelihood of another pathogen with even deadlier potential than COVID-19 remains.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have four points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the responsibility of parents and guardians.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 2A places responsibility on parents and guardians to ensure that an individual with an intellectual disability or who otherwise lacks mental capacity to comply with requirements under the Infectious Disease Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The parent or guardian may be served with a notice to ensure the compliance of the individual.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The parent or guardian may be found liable for an offence if they fail to ensure that the individual complies with any requirement of the Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the Mental Capacity Act, there are certain principles to balance a person’s right to make their own decisions and the need to protect them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These principles include that before an act is done or a decision is made, it must be considered whether the purpose of the act or decision can be effectively achieved in a way that is less restrictive of the person’s rights and freedom of action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another principle is that a person must be assumed to have capacity unless it is established that the person lacks capacity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A further principle is that a person is not to be treated as unable to make a decision merely because the person makes an unwise decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When a parent or guardian is served with a notice to ensure compliance of the individual, the measures taken to ensure compliance may involve some restriction of rights or freedom of action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify whether these principles under the Mental Capacity Act continue to apply when the parent or guardian is served with a notice to ensure the compliance of the individual with requirements under the Infectious Diseases Act?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How should a parent or guardian of an individual lacking mental capacity balance their responsibilities under the Infectious Diseases Act and the principles they must abide under the Mental Capacity Act?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As Asst Prof Dr Rayner Tan from the National University of Singapore (NUS) Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health argued in a recent CNA commentary, stigma and a lack of access to prevention methods stand in the way of an HIV-free future.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The 2023 Global Update by the Joint United Nations (UN) Programme on HIV and AIDS has also found that punitive laws are more likely to drive people away from seeking HIV support and services and may be counterproductive to public health efforts.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If so, can the Government explain its decision to tweak section 23 instead of entirely repealing this law?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In that case, the Judge held that even though the accused had only been informed by the Public Health Officer working at the National Public Health Unit that he was required to disclose his HIV-positive status to his sexual partners, the Public Health Officer's opinion of the law was not conclusive.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Instead, the High Court held that the plain language of section 23 means that a person must communicate the risk of contracting HIV and not merely one's HIV status.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This judgement has caused confusion among people who are subject to the disclosure obligation under section 23 as to what would satisfy this requirement to communicate the risk of contracting HIV.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What steps have or will the Government take to clarify the ambiguity in section 23?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can the Government provide an update on the number of complaints it has received and the number of investigations it has conducted under this law since it was introduced in 2008?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can the Government also confirm if, in light of medical advances, the reasonable precautions under section 23(2)(c) will include the correct use of pre-exposure prophylaxis, also known as PrEP?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If so, would the Government consider amending this sub clause to remove the phrase during the sexual activity and or explicitly recognise the use of PrEP as reasonable precaution?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If not, can the Government explain why not?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members have sought clarifications on the proposed amendments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Louis Ng sought clarifications on how the guardian of an individual who lacks mental capacity should balance their responsibilities under the Infectious Diseases Act (IDA) and the principles under the Mental Capacity Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The principles under the Mental Capacity Act will therefore continue to apply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Under the new section 2A, the IDA notice must first be served on the minor or individual.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Where the minor or individual is not able to fully understand and follow through with the requirements in the IDA notice, the same IDA notice is then served on the parent or guardian, requiring them to facilitate the minor or individual’s compliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a reasonable expectation, that the parent or guardian should play a part.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Section 2A allows the Ministry of Health (MOH) to take action in cases of irresponsible parents or guardians, who without reasonable excuse, fail to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ng asked about the safeguards for the management of information collected from classes of persons under section 7.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The current section 7 already allows the Director-General of Health (DGH) to require any person to provide information for the purposes of public health surveillance, epidemiological investigations or surveys.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The amendment is not an expansion of powers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Rather, it clarifies and makes explicit the manner in which DGH may exercise his power to require information from classes of persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, a notice can be issued to the class of “persons who are in charge of a laboratory”, as opposed to multiple individual notices issued to each person in charge of a laboratory.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It may be necessary to match the samples collected to the data collected for the right patient.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But where data can be used in anonymised form, such as to conduct trend analysis, MOH will do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH treats the management and protection of personal data very seriously, regardless of whether the information is collected from individuals or a class of persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Sensitive personal data is managed and protected in compliance with whole-of-Government standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Disclosure of information under the IDA requires DGH’s authorisation and is only for public health purposes, including measures to prevent and control an outbreak and national public health research.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: DGH may also impose additional conditions on the receiving party to better protect the information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In relation to section 15 on the detection and isolation of persons, Mr Ng pointed out that while an individual may be ordered to be isolated in his own residence "for the protection of the public", this phrase is not used in relation to individuals being ordered to isolate in a hospital.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The difference in language is not new and already exists in the current Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Isolation of persons in a hospital protects other patients and hospital staff, whereas isolation of individuals in their residence is more directly for the protection of the public within the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On whether MOH considered providing for a time limit for isolation orders under section 15, the duration of a section 15 isolation order is not open ended or arbitrary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic and also in the context of other communicable diseases, the duration has always been based on public health considerations and grounded in medical science, typically until the individual is no longer infectious or potentially infectious.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I note that Mr Louis Ng as well as Ms He Ting Ru welcomed the provisions in relation to HIV.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ng asked about the definition of undetectable viral load, length of the prescribed period and whether these would be periodically updated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms He Ting Ru has also raised some other questions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In response, I would say that section 23 remains relevant to reduce sexual transmission of HIV, by requiring persons living with HIV with a detectable viral load and persons who do not know of their status, but have reasons to believe that they have HIV, to disclose their risk of acquiring HIV to their sexual partners prior to sexual activity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This allows sexual partners to make an informed decision before engaging in sexual activities and to encourage responsible sexual behaviour by taking mitigating measures such as ensuring condom use to protect themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The intention of the HIV laws is not to criminalise persons living with HIV, but to deter irresponsible behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She had also made reference to the high court judgment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The high court judgment will be superseded by the amendment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The law at that time was that a person living with HIV was required to inform their sexual partners of the risk of getting HIV infection from them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This law was informed by the state of medical science and there have since been developments in this, and that is why we are updating the laws to align with these developments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Third, they had adhered to medical treatment for HIV infection up to the time of the sexual activity in question.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: COVID-19 will not be the last pandemic that we encounter.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I just want to add a comment to the amendment to section 23.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are keeping section 23 because it is still relevant for those who are infected, or think that they are infected, that they continue to have an obligation to inform.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, the Bill provides an exemption for those who have tested, sought treatment and then lower themselves to an undetectable and untransmissible level.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We think this combination best protects public health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Other countries might have come to a different combination, but MOH has studied together with the experts, and we find that this combination probably best protects public health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam has answered all questions, I have nothing further to add.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for the Minister and Senior Parliamentary Secretary?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I have a clarification to ask of Minister for Health Mr Ong Ye Kung.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: With the new Act and the new classifications of public health threat and public health emergency, a number of Clementi residents will be wondering what becomes of the older DORSCON classification – the Disease Outbreak Response System Condition Classification.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: A number of residents had shared that the different colours green, yellow, orange and red can mean different things to different people.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, can the Minister advise us what will become of DORSCON now that we have the clearer status of public health threat and public health emergency.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That was a very good question from Clementi residents.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: DORSCON stands for Disease Outbreak Response System Condition, it has four colours.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It was used by the Public Service for agencies to coordinate response and to plan resources.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But during COVID-19, somehow it became an external communication code and it triggered all kinds of reactions in supermarkets.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: The first is, I thank Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam for saying that the amendment supersedes the ruling in GCP vs Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I acknowledge that amendment supersedes the court sentencing framework.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: However, I am not clear about the use of the interpretation of meaning of risk of disclosing HIV.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: So, I would like to ask for further clarifications about that.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: What specifically in particular are the persons living with HIV are supposed to do in that context.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: The second point that I wanted to seek further clarifications on is that I do not believe that there is any local study on the effectiveness of criminalisation of HIV non-disclosure on reducing HIV infection rates, albeit this time where we are talking about a reduced group of people that this applies to.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I am just wondering what can MOH do to address the potential stigma that might arise from this continued criminalisation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, when at that juncture, the strongest evidence for adherence of medical treatment would be the UVL test result from a recognised laboratory at the next regular medical follow-up visit for HIV after the sexual activity in question because it will show that they have maintained their UVL, as this would not have been possible without treatment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There would be other circumstantial evidence for adherence to treatment that may include contemporaneous records at the next follow-up visit after the sexual activity in question, of documented treatment adherence, or documentation in past medical records of a consistent pattern of treatment adherence and consistent past UVL test results carried out by a recognised laboratory.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are the things that they would have to show in the event there is a complaint made and investigations follow.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In as far as how they would conduct themselves, the reality is that this is a law, a provision that says you are not supposed to do it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, if they then do this and there is a complaint made, investigations will follow, and these are the provisions and the evidence that they can rely on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is the premise upon which we are making this change.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In contrast, other sexual activities, although lower risk, pose some transmission risk.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we will not want to change our position completely on this because what we are doing is based on data, based on evidence, and requiring disclosure of the risk of acquiring HIV prior to sexual activity so as to allow the sexual partners to make an informed decision before engaging in sexual activities, and be able to then take the mitigating measures, such as medications, to protect themselves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any other clarifications for the Minister and the Senior Parliamentary Secretary?
